ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Consider an optical system made of many identical ideal (negligible-thickness) halflenses with focal length $f>0$, organized so that they share the same center and are angular-separated equally at density $n$ (number of lenses per unit-radian). Define the length-scale $\lambda=f / n$. A light-ray arrives perpendicular to the first lens at distance $\lambda / 2$ away from the center, then leaves from the last lens at distance $2 \lambda$ away from the center. Estimate the total deflection angle (in rad) of the light-ray by this system in the limit $n \rightarrow \infty$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, many black half-lenses/half-lens segments are arranged in a fan shape outward from the same center, and n→∞ is labeled, indicating that the angular spacing tends to a continuum. An orange light ray enters horizontally from the left and strikes the first vertical lens perpendicularly; the distance from the incident point to the center is labeled λ/2. After passing through the fan-shaped lens system, the light ray exits on the right near the radius position labeled 2λ and is deflected toward the lower right. Reasoning: According to the specified method, first take λ=1, so f=n and the angular spacing h=1/n. Let the angular position of the k-th radial lens be s_k=kh, the local radial direction be e_r(s_k), and the local optical axis direction be e_s(s_k). Write the ray direction after passing through the k-th lens as e_s+p e_r, where p is the local slope. The thin-lens action gives the slope kick p→p-r/n=p-hr. When propagating from one lens to the next radial half-line with angular spacing h, the geometric intersection relation gives r_{k+1}=r_k/(cos h-p_k sin h), while the local slope before reaching the next lens is p^-_{k+1}=(sin h+p_k cos h)/(cos h-p_k sin h). After another thin-lens kick: p_{k+1}=p^-_{k+1}-h r_{k+1}. Initially r_0=1/2, and the incident direction is perpendicular to the first lens, so the initial local slope in the continuous limit is p(0)=0. Letting h→0, the above discrete ray tracing gives the continuous equations dr/ds=rp, dp/ds=1+p^2-r, with initial conditions r(0)=1/2, p(0)=0. Eliminating s: dp/dr=(1+p^2-r)/(rp). Let y=1+p^2, then dy/dr=2(y-r)/r. The solution is y=2r+Cr^2. From the initial condition r=1/2, p=0, get C=0, so 1+p^2=2r. Therefore p=sqrt(2r-1). When the ray exits, r=2, so p=sqrt(3). The angle swept by the fan of lenses is s_*=∫_{1/2}^{2} dr/[r sqrt(2r-1)]. Let u=sqrt(2r-1), then r=(1+u^2)/2, and the integral becomes s_*=∫_0^{sqrt(3)} 2 du/(1+u^2)=2 arctan(sqrt(3))=2π/3. Finally, the local slope p=sqrt(3) corresponds to an angle arctan(sqrt(3))=π/3 relative to the local optical axis. Since the local optical axis has rotated by 2π/3 relative to the initial horizontal optical axis, the final global direction has angle -(2π/3)+π/3=-π/3 relative to the initial horizontal line. Therefore the magnitude of the total deflection angle is π/3≈1.047 rad, estimated as 1.05 rad according to the problem requirement.
